review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked whether Mathlib already has a simp lemma for `a +ᵥ Ici 0`. The file declares no simp lemmas, no simp attributes and no `@[simp]` rewrites, so it has no simp-orientation problems, competing rules, unwanted expansions or cycles. The only simp uses are local `simp only [...]` and `simpa` calls that close small goals.

The `hset : a +ᵥ Ici 0 = Ici a` proof is written out twice, in `comp_add_const` and in `iteratedDerivWithin_Ici_comp_add_const`. That is duplication, not a simp-interface defect. I did not make it a finding because `Ici` shifts are better served by an explicit helper than by a global simp lemma, and the rubric asks me not to recommend simp attributes just because an identity looks simple.

`iteratedDerivWithin_Ici_comp_add_const` has hypotheses (`0 ≤ a`, `0 ≤ t`, `ContDiffOn`) and is a conditional equality. It would be a poor simp lemma, since simp would have to discharge those side conditions in the uses I read, and I found no use that needs it as one. I found no evidence of a practical simp-interface improvement. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out simp behavior I did not read.
